name: Langston Hughes
bio: Langston Hughes was a central figure in the Harlem Renaissance and one of the most influential African American writers of the 20th century. His plays at the Greenwich Mews Theater brought Black experience to integrated audiences during the height of the Civil Rights movement.

name: Stella Holt
bio: Stella Holt was the visionary founder and longtime director of the Greenwich Mews Theater. Her commitment to interracial casting and socially conscious drama made the Mews a unique space in American theater during the segregation era.

name: Ossie Davis
bio: Ossie Davis was a legendary actor, writer, and activist whose career was deeply intertwined with the Civil Rights movement. His work at the Greenwich Mews helped establish it as a home for Black theater artists.

name: Ruby Dee
bio: Ruby Dee was an acclaimed actress and civil rights activist who, along with her husband Ossie Davis, brought powerful performances to the Greenwich Mews stage. Her presence helped legitimize the theater as a serious artistic venue.

name: Loften Mitchell
bio: Loften Mitchell was a playwright and historian whose work chronicled the African American experience in theater. His plays at the Greenwich Mews addressed racial injustice and the Black experience in America.

name: Alice Childress
bio: Alice Childress was a groundbreaking playwright and novelist whose work gave voice to working-class Black women. Her association with the Greenwich Mews helped establish her as a major American dramatist.
